verbs.name: core.edit_document
verbs.effectReason: its UPDATE runs inside `update_document`, and `set_representation` re-points the body at freshly minted bytes.

verbs.name: core.replace_document_content
verbs.effectReason: `update_document` plus `set_representation`: one document, a new body.

verbs.name: core.set_extracted_text
verbs.effectReason: `upsert_text_derivative` fills in an existing document's text; no row a member names appears.

verbs.name: core.merge_party
verbs.effectReason: `fold_party` moves every reference onto the survivor and trashes the loser — not the `Delete` its SQL would look like.

verbs.name: locker.star_item
verbs.effectReason: `set_starred` carries the UPDATE.

verbs.name: locker.unstar_item
verbs.effectReason: `set_starred` carries the UPDATE.

verbs.name: locker.counts
verbs.effectReason: counts the locker's rows and writes nothing.

verbs.name: locker.totp_code
verbs.effectReason: derives a code from a stored seed and writes only its subject receipt.

verbs.name: locker.watchtower
verbs.effectReason: reports weak and reused secrets; writes only its subject receipt.

verbs.name: locker.export
verbs.effectReason: reads every item and writes only the one receipt the mass reveal owes; what makes it grave is its egress, not its effect.

verbs.name: locker.reveal_receipt
verbs.effectReason: records that a seat-side reveal happened; `access_receipt` is append-only and is not a row a member names.

verbs.name: media.add_asset
verbs.effectReason: mints an asset and its content item; identical bytes dedupe onto one.

verbs.name: media.derive_missing
verbs.effectReason: fills in derivatives for assets that already exist; no new asset appears.

verbs.name: media.set_favorite
verbs.effectReason: `set_starred` carries the UPDATE.

verbs.name: people.star_person
verbs.effectReason: `set_starred` carries the UPDATE.

verbs.name: people.unstar_person
verbs.effectReason: `set_starred` carries the UPDATE.

verbs.name: people.move_person
verbs.effectReason: `file_into_list` re-files an existing party.

verbs.name: people.add_note
verbs.effectReason: `annotate` mints the journal note the member then names.

verbs.name: people.add_task
verbs.effectReason: `task_for_person` mints a task and links it to the party.

verbs.name: people.add_gift
verbs.effectReason: `task_for_person` mints a task and links it to the party.

verbs.name: schedule.set_task_status
verbs.effectReason: one command that completes, cancels or reopens depending on `status`: the registry fixes no single effect, only the argument does.

verbs.name: tally.add_group_member
verbs.effectReason: `add_circle_member` mints the circle membership the group reads back.

verbs.name: tally.add_expense
verbs.effectReason: `write_new_expense` mints the expense, its payers and its splits.

verbs.name: tally.add_receipt_expense
verbs.effectReason: the same mint as `tally.add_expense`, from a receipt's line items.

verbs.name: tally.reallocate_receipt
verbs.effectReason: `write_line_items` and `write_splits` re-cut an expense that already exists.

verbs.name: tally.materialize_recurring_expense
verbs.effectReason: mints this occurrence of a recurring expense as a real one.

egress.$note: `egressVerbs` is the set a refusal class is built from: every command whose declared egress is not `none`. `exec.rs` reads it through `canon::egress_verbs()` and holds no list of its own.

locker.add_item.why: `online_only` and sealed-input: the seat seals the secret before the gateway sees it. Nothing leaves.

locker.duplicate_item.why: copies one item's sealed cells to a second row inside the same vault; the ciphertext never leaves.

locker.edit_item.why: as `locker.add_item` — the seat seals, the vault stores.

locker.export.why: every secret the locker holds, in the clear, in a file the seat writes.

locker.reveal_receipt.why: records that a seat revealed something. The reveal left custody; writing down that it did, did not.

locker.rotate_key.why: `online_only` because the seat holds the key it rotates; the new key never leaves that seat.

locker.set_field.why: as `locker.add_item` — the seat seals, the vault stores.

locker.set_passkey.why: as `locker.add_item` — the seat seals the private key, the vault stores it.

locker.totp_code.why: derives a code at the member's own seat; it is shown, not sent.

locker.watchtower.why: reads the locker's own rows and answers at the seat.

social.draft_message.why: a draft is a row and stays one; sending it is `social.send_message`.

social.send_message.why: the member's request is for the message to ARRIVE; the row it records is the vault's half of a transfer.

tally.materialize_recurring_expense.why: `online_only` so the recurrence plane is reachable, not because anything is handed out.

tally.nudge.why: writes one row saying a reminder was PREPARED, with `sent` stated and always false, because no delivery path exists.

owed_to_me.gap: People ships no obligation reader. `tally.obligation` is in this app's read scopes and no query returns a per-party total; the field's only implementation is the eval harness's reference reader, which is the thing being evaluated (DIFF.md B6).

owed_to_them.gap: As `owed_to_me`, the other direction. No shipped reader (DIFF.md B7).

next_occurrence.gap: The next anniversary of a `month_day`. The dates board sorts by the stored columns and never projects the next occurrence; no shipped reader computes it (DIFF.md B5).

member_party_ids.gap: A group's members are reached through `social.circle_member`, and no shipped query hands the id list back beside the group row; the grammar's Field is served only by the eval harness (DIFF.md B4). It is also the two-hop walk DIFF.md B12 records.

unanchored.$note: A polymorphic (X_type, X_id) pair the DDL does not hold to `core_entity` with a composite foreign key. Nothing constrains the id to a row that exists, or ever existed. Found by the role check, reported and not fixed: whether each is a receipt that MUST outlive its object or a pointer at a row that is gone is the owner's ruling, and the DDL is not this lane's to change.

pairs.reading: deliberate — provenance says where a row CAME FROM, and a purge that erased the record of the import would erase the only answer to `why is this here`. It is also outside the 96, so no role carries it.
deliberate — the receipt plane is append-only and hash-chained by `seq`. A receipt that vanished with its object is not a receipt (D-1020-L3 says so for the Locker reveal in as many words).

gap — a seed row names a planted row and nothing keeps the two in step, so a purged fixture leaves a seed row pointing at an id that was never reissued. Low stakes, machinery only; an anchor with `ON DELETE CASCADE` is what the other thirteen edges have.
deliberate — evidence is what an agent CITED at the time, and it has to read back after the cited row is gone or the audit answers nothing.

split — deliberate against TRASH (an undo must read the prior state of a row that is in the bin), a gap against PURGE: nothing prunes a revision when its entity is purged, so `tally.undo_expense` can be offered a revision of a row that no longer exists in any sense. The owner's call is whether purge should cascade here.

gap, and the sharpest of the seven — an authority is a live capability, and `(subject_type, subject_id)` unanchored means a grant can outlive its subject and be served against an id the vault has since reissued to something else.

judgements.around Num: not derivable — the ontology marks no column as an estimate. GRAMMAR.md §2.4's band on `effort_min` is a product ruling; the schema would need a granularity or `estimate` annotation for it to fall out.
